channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Consolidates below mid-1.3500s; bullish potential seems intact
item.description: The GBP/USD pair struggles to capitalize on the previous day's modest gains and oscillates in a range below mid-1.3500s during the Asian session on Tuesday. The downside, however, remains cushioned as the US Dollar (USD) selling remains unabated on the back of a broadly firmer Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: New Zealand Dollar struggles after China’s Trade Balance data
item.description: NZD/USD extends its losses for the third successive day, trading around 0.5850 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The pair is depreciating as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains under pressure following the release of trade data from China, New Zealand’s major trading partner.

item.title: Euro holds steady above 1.1600 as markets brace for US inflation data and ECB rate decision
item.description: The EUR/USD pair trades on a flat note around 1.1625 during the early European trading hours on Tuesday. Traders prefer to wait on the sidelines ahead of the key US inflation data and the European Central Bank (ECB) interest rate decision later this week.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices rose in India on Tuesday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD jumps to near $67 amid drop in US Dollar, bond yields
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is up 1.25% to near $67.00 during the Asian trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold benefits from weak USD; eyes $4,450 as focus remains on US CPI data
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) attracts some buyers during the Asian session on Tuesday, snapping a two-day losing streak as the recent US Dollar (USD) pullback from a three-week high gains momentum amid the rallying Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: RBA’s Hunter: Housing market crucial transition channel for monetary policy
item.description: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Assistant Governor Hunter said on Tuesday that the housing market is an important transition mechanism for monetary policy. Hunter added that the central bank is looking to cool things off in both the housing market and the broader economy.

item.title: Iran's warns economic warfare will be met by maritime exclusion zone
item.description: Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, warned on Tuesday that Tehran would respond to what it calls US "economic warfare" by imposing a maritime exclusion zone across the Persian Gulf.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains steady following China’s Trade Balance data
item.description: AUD/USD halts its four-day winning streak, trading around 0.7210 during Asian hours on Tuesday. The pair holds ground following the release Trade Balance data from China, Australia’s close trading partner.

item.title: China’s August Trade Balance: Surplus widens to $119.09 billion as expected
item.description: China's Trade Balance for August, in US Dollar (USD) terms, arrives at $119.09 billion, almost in line with $119.1 billion estimates, but higher than the July reading of $112.5 billion.

item.title: US Dollar Index (DXY) struggles below 99.00, two-week low as traders eye US inflation data
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, remains under some selling pressure for the second straight day and drops to an over two-week low during the Asian session on Tuesday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains as US Dollar struggles despite rising Fed rate hike bets
item.description: USD/CAD extends its losses for the second successive day, trading around 1.3800 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. Analysts at HSBC caution that, despite the recent improvement in sentiment around the Fed’s anti-inflation stance, broader structural issues have not disappeared.

item.title: British Pound drifts higher to near 1.3550 on UK fiscal discipline pledges
item.description: The GBP/USD pair gains ground to near 1.3545 during the Asian trading hours on Tuesday. The British Pound (GBP) edges higher against the US Dollar (USD) after UK Chancellor John Healey unveiled a series of measures designed to encourage economic growth and draw more private investment into the UK.

item.title: WTI slips below $90.50 despite rising Middle East supply risks
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price edges lower and is trading around $90.40 per barrel during Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen rallies to February 18 high as upbeat wage data and GDP lift BoJ hike bets
item.description: The USD/JPY pair declines for the second straight day – also marking the fourth day of a fall in the previous five – and sinks to its lowest level since February 18, around mid-153.00s during the Asian session on Tuesday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7804 vs. 6.7795 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Tuesday at 6.7804 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7795 and 6.7104 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro holds gains above 1.1600 on ECB tightening prospects
item.description: The EUR/USD pair trades with mild gains around 1.1625 during the early Asian session on Tuesday. The Euro (EUR) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) amid expectations of a rate hike from the European Central Bank (ECB).

item.title: Gold declines to near $4,400 as robust US jobs data lifts Fed hike odds
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) drifts lower to near $4,410 during the early Asian session on Tuesday. The precious metal extends the decline as a stronger-than-expected US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report for August bolsters expectations for a Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike this month.

item.title: Citi Survey sees Banxico frozen as Peso holds below 18.00
item.description: Citi Mexico released its September “Expectations Survey,” in which most private economists expect the Bank of Mexico (Banxico) to hold rates unchanged, while the exchange rate is forecast to end below the 18.00 threshold by the end of 2026.

item.title: Thai Baht: Recent THB gains face headwinds – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Christopher Wong notes that recent Thai Baht (THB) strength may slow as external conditions turn less supportive. Governor Vitai’s comments suggest further rate cuts are unlikely without another shock, tempering easing expectations.

item.title: Australian Dollar rides thin-trading lift as Fed test looms
item.description: The Aussie Dollar climbed for the fourth straight day, up 0.22% against the US Dollar, amid thin volumes as US financial markets were closed in observance of the Labour Day Holiday. The AUD/USD trades at 0.7218, after bouncing off daily lows of 0.7194.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Hong Kong’s offshore gateway role expands – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay highlights Hong Kong’s first five-year plan to strengthen its position as the leading offshore CNY and cross-border financial centre.

item.title: The Canadian Dollar gains as Oil rally offsets jobs gloom
item.description: The Loonie gains some traction versus the Greenback, while the latter posts modest losses, as US and Canadian financial markets remain closed in observance of Labour Day. Nevertheless, the USD/CAD edges lower by some 0.15%, trading at 1.3813 at the time of writing.

item.title: South Korean Won: Authorities signal pause in KRW strength – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner reports that USD/KRW rebounded from 1335 after news that Korea’s National Pension Service may halt or reverse its forward-market Dollar selling. Authorities appear comfortable with recent Won gains after a 15% USD/KRW drop since June.

item.title: Tuesday tells the Japanese Yen more than next week will
item.description: USD/JPY trades just above 154.00 after giving up 1.22% on a Monday with American desks shut. Everything the pair has left to argue about arrives inside ten days, and the first of it lands tonight.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Oil and US inflation pose risks – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan warns that upcoming US inflation data could test the recent Rupiah recovery, as firmer US inflation may reinforce elevated US yields and challenge USD/IDR’s break below 17,700.

item.title: Pound Sterling's rate advantage buys it no say this week
item.description: GBP/USD holds just under 1.3550 after a Monday that covered 42 pips with American desks shut for Labor Day. The week that follows is not that.

item.title: Vietnam: Inflation and trade trends shape VND – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Vietnam update highlights rising inflation and a narrowing trade deficit, with strong manufacturing-led imports and resilient exports. The bank notes elevated CPI and external deficits limit scope for aggressive easing, but robust activity persists.

item.title: Mexican Peso stumbles as traders brace for US inflation week
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) loses some ground versus its North American counterpart, the US Dollar (USD), as the USD/MXN pair rises over 0.25% to 16.93, even though the Greenback edges lower against a basket of six currencies, the so-called US Dollar Index (DXY).

item.title: A German landslide moved the Euro by nothing at all
item.description: EUR/USD holds above 1.1600, seven pips above where Monday opened. The pair has had three chances to move over four sessions and has taken none of them. Both central banks are priced to raise rates this month for the same energy shock, and a rate gap that is not moving does not move a currency.
